hook
Your fridge doesn't make cold. It actually steals heat! Here's how.
parts
Hidden inside is a loop of pipe, filled with a special liquid called refrigerant.
parts
It flows through four parts. A compressor, hot coils at the back, a tiny valve, and cold coils inside.
evap
Inside the fridge, the refrigerant boils into a gas, even below freezing.
evap
Just like sweat cooling your skin, evaporating soaks up heat, pulling warmth out of your food.
comp
Next, the compressor squeezes this gas tightly. Squeezing makes it really hot.
cond
The hot gas flows through the coils at the back, and gives its heat away to your kitchen.
cond
As it cools down, it turns back into a liquid.
valve
Then it squeezes through a tiny valve. The pressure suddenly drops, and the liquid becomes ice cold.
loop
And the loop starts all over again, carrying heat out, again and again.
fact
That's why the back of your fridge feels warm, and why it hums when the compressor runs.
tip
So don't leave the door open. Warm air rushes in, and the motor has to work much harder.
outro
Your fridge is really a heat mover. Follow for more science behind everyday things!
